overview: The notification service validates the request, checks preferences (cached), dedups on an idempotency key, renders the template and enqueues to the channel's SQS queue. Channel workers call the provider with exponential backoff; after 5 attempts messages go to the DLQ.

estimation.calculation: 10,000,000 / 600 ≈ 16,667 deliveries/s before retries and multiple channels.
estimation.result: Provider quotas may be lower than application enqueue throughput.
estimation.implication: Separate channel queues/consumer groups and enforce provider-specific rate limits.

flows.title: Validate and fan out by channel

steps.title: Internal services → Gateway → Notification Service → Preferences cache
steps.explanation: Authorize caller and evaluate channel consent/quiet hours.

steps.title: Notification Service → Notifications DB
steps.explanation: Record logical notification and outbox with a unique idempotency key.

steps.title: Notification Service → Email queue → Email workers → SES
steps.explanation: Deliver an email with provider-specific rate limits; other channel workers operate independently.

steps.title: Push queue → Push workers → APNs/FCM
steps.explanation: On retryable failure use exponential backoff; persist attempt identity and eventually move to a DLQ. Do not retry permanent opt-out/address failures.

failureCases.scenario: Provider times out after accepting a message
failureCases.handling: Retry using provider idempotency where supported; retain the ambiguous attempt and provider request ID. Bound retries with backoff and a DLQ; do not promise universal exactly-once delivery.

alternatives: Use channel queues for operational simplicity and failure isolation. Use Kafka topics for replay, ordered partitions and independent consumers, accepting lag management and retry-topic complexity.
